Two of three runs were fallbacks, and the primary run was not the one that published the episode

The primary run started at 1:05 AM Pacific and completed at 1:33 AM Pacific with a success conclusion. Fallback 1 (2:05 AM Pacific) also completed successfully. The script came in under target and shipped under target

The first draft was 2,407 words against a 3,400-word target. It was sent back for one expand pass, and the shipped script is 3,100 words. The episode is still 300 words short of target, which is the thin-day case the pipeline tolerates. The episode's word count is well above the length the pipeline counts as short under SHORT_EPISODE_WORDS.

The cold open was skipped because it ran 91 words, which exceeded the length limit. Listeners heard the episode without it. Consider raising the cold-open word limit if this recurs on normal nights, since skipping it removes the framing the show normally opens with.

The roundup pool kept 18 stories: 16 local and 2 theme. Of 39 local stories available, 16 aired. The roundup opened local, and the deep dives all led with local subjects, with one Cariboo deep dive. Six on-theme candidates were not used. The airtime budget (NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT) cut 55 stories from the roundup pool; those stories remain eligible for a later, better-matched day.

Theme loading, by contrast, was not the constraint: 52 theme articles loaded against 51 bonus articles. The bottleneck was airtime, not the feed. If the theme should carry more of the roundup, raise its share of NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT rather than widening the pool.

The text-to-speech canary timed out and OpenAI rendered the whole episode

Two of the short TTS takes were retried, and both retries came back short again. The longer take of each was kept, so no content was dropped, but the audio for those two takes is shorter than their word count predicts. This is a single observation about two takes, not a missing segment.

What happened

Two degradations shaped the audio and the script

The script's Kagi Extract step returned no matching page for 6 of 6 URLs sent, so the script was written without the extracted article text it normally draws on. The pipeline did not stop; it went on to write from the feed material alone. The listener gets the same show structure, but the detail behind the four deep-dive stories comes from fewer sources than usual.

Separately, a name in the script, ʔEten, has no entry in config/pronunciations.json, so the text-to-speech engine guessed at its pronunciation. Add the entry before the next run that names it.

The roundup opened on local news and cut 21 stories

The roundup pool held 18 stories after deduplication, and the airtime budget (NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT) dropped 21 more. The pool is designed to be larger than one segment can air, so the cut is expected; the dropped stories can return on a day that matches them better. The roundup aired 5 local stories against 4 available, and it opened with local news. Nothing was split across subjects.

Of the 18 pooled stories, 12 of 18 roundup citations matched their sources. Of the 4 deep dives, 3 of 4 citations matched.

Four focus-routed articles were held and none released

The cycle is in week 2 of 4 on the Language & Culture focus. Four articles were routed to other focuses and held, and 0 were released for this focus, so the held articles are not in tonight's episode. Two are headed for The Living World and two for Mining & Energy. Their release dates are 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-24. Check that the held articles will be released on those dates; if the focus rotation is shorter than the holds, they will wait a full cycle.
